karpathy.en:
Had to go see Project Hail Mary right away (it's based on the book of Andy Weir, of also The Martian fame). Both very pleased and relieved to say that 1) the movie sticks very close to the book in both content and tone and 2) is really well executed.

The book is one of my favorites when it comes to alien portrayals because a lot of thought was clearly given to the scientific details of an alternate biochemistry, evolutionary history, sensorium, psychology, language, tech tree, etc. It's different enough that it is highly creative and plausible, but also similar enough that you get a compelling story and one of the best bromances in fiction. Not to mention the other (single-cellular) aliens. I can count fictional portrayals of aliens of this depth on one hand. A lot of these aspects are briefly featured - if you read the book you'll spot them but if you haven't, the movie can't spend the time to do them justice.

I'll say that the movie inches a little too much into the superhero movie tropes with the pacing, the quips, the Bathos and such for my taste, and we get a little bit less the grand of Interstellar and a little bit less of the science of The Martian, but I think it's ok considering the tone of the original content. And it does really well where it counts - on Rocky and the bromance. Thank you to the film crew for the gem!
karpathy.zh:
必须立即去看《万福玛丽计划》（它是根据《火星救援》中的安迪·威尔的书改编的）。两人都非常高兴和欣慰地说：1）这部电影在内容和基调上都与原著非常接近，2）执行得非常好。

当谈到外星人的描绘时，这本书是我最喜欢的书之一，因为它清楚地考虑了另一种生物化学、进化历史、感觉、心理学、语言、科技树等科学细节。它足够不同，具有高度的创造性和合理性，但也足够相似，你可以得到一个引人入胜的故事和小说中最好的兄弟情谊之一。更不用说其他（单细胞）外星人了。我一只手就能数出如此深度的外星人的虚构描绘。其中很多方面都进行了简要介绍——如果你读过这本书，你就会发现它们，但如果你没有，电影就不会花时间来公正地呈现它们。

我想说的是，这部电影在节奏、俏皮话、巴托斯等方面有点过于融入超级英雄电影的比喻，对我来说，我们得到的《星际穿越》的宏大和《火星救援》的科学知识也少了一点，但考虑到原始内容的基调，我认为这还可以。它在重要的地方表现得非常好——洛基和兄弟情谊。感谢摄制组的宝石！

petergyang.en:
I think OpenAI’s strategy is pretty clear:

1. More people have ChatGPT installed than any other AI product

2. Make ChatGPT great for coding and knowledge work

3. Make it a personal assistant like OpenClaw that knows you and can do whatever you want 

They just need to do 2 and 3 faster before people switch to Claude or Gemini for the same use cases.
petergyang.zh:
我认为 OpenAI 的策略非常明确：

1.安装ChatGPT的人比任何其他人工智能产品都多

2. 让 ChatGPT 非常适合编码和知识工作

3. 让它成为一个像OpenClaw一样了解你并且可以做你想做的事情的私人助理 

他们只需要更快地完成 2 和 3 步，然后人们就相同的用例转向 Claude 或 Gemini。

levie.en:
Without getting into the specific numbers, this underlying concept and trend is going to be very real. For any worker who is able to wield AI agents effectively in an organization, their compute budgets are just going to monotonically go up over time. 

This will of course start in engineering, where we already know developers can run multiple agents in parallel, or have projects going over night. But this eventually hit the rest of knowledge work as well. Lawyers that can create and review more drafts, marketed that can build more campaigns and test more ideals in parallel, sales reps that can reach out to more customers and process more leads. 

Many of these activities will essentially be token-dependent in how much work a single person can do. These aren’t chatbot workflows answering a simple question, but agents that are running and processing through incredible amounts of data at scale, and generating all new forms of information.

Companies will have to figure out how they budget for this, and it likely won’t be an IT budget item over time, but ultimately owned and allocated by the business. Maybe the CFO is ultimately the head of AI :-).
levie.zh:
在不考虑具体数字的情况下，这一基本概念和趋势将是非常真实的。对于任何能够在组织中有效使用人工智能代理的员工来说，他们的计算预算只会随着时间的推移而单调增加。 

这当然将从工程开始，我们已经知道开发人员可以并行运行多个代理，或者让项目连夜进行。但这最终也影响了其他知识工作。律师可以创建和审查更多草稿，营销人员可以开展更多活动并同时测试更多理想，销售代表可以接触更多客户并处理更多潜在客户。 

其中许多活动本质上取决于一个人可以完成多少工作。这些不是回答简单问题的聊天机器人工作流程，而是大规模运行和处理大量数据并生成所有新形式信息的代理。

公司必须弄清楚如何为此进行预算，而且随着时间的推移，它可能不会成为 IT 预算项目，而是最终由企业拥有和分配。也许首席财务官最终是人工智能的负责人:-)。

nikunj.en:
I *think* the tide is finally going to turn on all the actors (LPs, VCs, founders, employees) who believe momentum is simply everything.. 

It has led to terrible trickle down effects across the entire ecosystem (manipulating data, no diligence, growth at all costs etc.)

As they say, what goes up must eventually come down. I hope these are not infamous last words, but I’m hopeful 🤞
nikunj.zh:
我“认为”这股潮流最终将转向所有相信动力就是一切的参与者（有限合伙人、风险投资人、创始人、员工）。 

它给整个生态系统带来了可怕的涓滴效应（操纵数据、不勤奋、不惜一切代价增长等）

正如他们所说，有涨必有跌。我希望这些不是臭名昭著的遗言，但我充满希望🤞
